name: Ridam Agrawal
long: Ridam Agrawal is a founding engineer in Indore and the sole developer at Dekho, a live-shopping app, working mostly on AI-powered products. Before Dekho: sole engineer on three production systems, a 23-agent multi-tenant SEO platform, the backend for a live broadcast competition app synced over WebSockets, and an internal operations suite.

front.motto: Ridam Agrawal’s paper of record, est. in a coffee cup
front.deck: Indore’s founding engineer builds startups their technology from the first line, and keeps a human hand on everything the machines write.

breaking.head: 350,000 users move house overnight
breaking.body: Not one of them noticed. Zero downtime, no data lost, witnesses confirm.

breaking.head: Twenty-three AI agents found sharing one pipeline
breaking.body: They crawl, research, write and publish off a single queue. The union has yet to comment.

breaking.head: Three production systems, one engineer
breaking.body: Asked who else was on the team, sources say: nobody.

coffee.head: Off the clock, a home barista

plate1.caption: The human hand is Michelangelo’s, c. 1512. The other is arithmetic, waiting for it.

issue.headline: The launch issue
issue.sub: Six products, from an empty repository to a live address.
issue.letter: Every picture in this issue is a product’s own front page, and every address under one is live. Where a project turned up a bug worth telling, the story is in Writing, at the back of the paper.

coverLines.text: What ChatGPT says about your business
Free advice that won’t give you a grade
Billing made for one hand and a busy counter

features.name: MasterChef
features.headline: The show must resume
features.standfirst: The official app for a broadcast cooking competition, with a backend built from scratch.
story: Contestants play along on their phones while the show streams live on Twitch, and every viewer sees that stream at a slightly different delay. The event flow runs over WebSockets and is timed to what each person can actually see.
Behind the scenes sit an admin console, video through Mux, email through SES and files on S3, on a backend he built as its only backend developer.
features.pull: Refresh, rejoin late or switch phones: the contest is where you left it.
features.credits: Sole backend developer · Set in Node.js, Express & MongoDB
features.imageAlt: The El Reto de MasterChef homepage: 'The next one could be you.' set over photos of contestants cooking.

features.name: KeySignals
features.headline: Does ChatGPT know your name?
features.standfirst: The company’s AI platform for search and AI answers, designed and built end to end by its only engineer.
story: Every page it writes starts from a profile of the business drawn from its own site, rather than from whatever a model happens to remember, and each task goes to Claude, OpenAI or Gemini, whichever suits it.

Publishing is not the end of it. It asks ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, AI Overviews and AI Mode whether the brand is named or cited, and a weekly pass over Search Console and Analytics drafts fixes for the pages that slip.
features.pull: The pages that slip get a fix, and the fix waits for a yes.
features.credits: Set in Next.js, PostgreSQL, Redis & BullMQ
features.imageAlt: The KeySignals homepage: 'Get found on Google and in AI answers', beside the product's dashboard for an example site.

features.name: PhaseDesk
features.headline: The standup nobody sits through
features.standfirst: An invite-only system that replaced the standups, timesheets and leave every project team used to keep by hand.
story: Each person writes one update a day: what was done, what is in progress, what is blocked. The timer, leave and the week’s report are all built from it.

Permissions are enforced in the API rather than the screen, across 13 data models. Reading across the whole organisation takes an explicit admin scope, and nothing is written to a project it cannot be attributed to.
features.pull: There is no sign-up page. An admin sends the invite.
features.credits: Set in Next.js, Express, Prisma & PostgreSQL
features.imageAlt: The PhaseDesk homepage: “Your team's day, written down once” beside an example daily update with completed work, work in progress and a blocker.

features.name: Elivate SEO Audit
features.headline: Same site, same report
features.standfirst: A technical audit for search and AI answers. Type a domain, and it reads the site the way a crawler does.
story: It reads the page, robots.txt, llms.txt and the sitemap, and reports across seven areas. There is no model and no paid API behind it, which is why the same site always gets the same report.
It also fetches whatever address a stranger types, so the fetcher is a guard first: it checks the address a name resolves to rather than the name, and checks again at every redirect.
features.pull: An address a stranger types is hostile until checked.
features.imageAlt: The Elivate SEO free site audit card: 'A fix for every finding, not a score.'

features.name: Easinvy Retail
features.headline: Below zero, on purpose
features.standfirst: Software for small Indian shops, where the screen is a phone held in one hand under shop lighting.
story: Bills, stock, purchases, customers and suppliers, staff attendance, sales reports and Razorpay subscriptions, for many shops at once, each with its own books.
Every number is the most legible thing on the screen. Stock is a running figure that can go negative, and the books treat that as information rather than an error.
features.credits: Set in Next.js, Express, Drizzle & PostgreSQL
features.imageAlt: The Easinvy Retail card: 'GST billing and stock, built for the counter', beside a sample GST bill.

features.name: SERP Reader
features.headline: A results page, saved as data
features.standfirst: A free Chrome extension, made to study which sources Google’s AI Overviews cite.
story: It was built to run the Elivate SEO study. It keeps the organic results, People Also Ask and the AI Overview’s citations as structured data, stored in the browser.
The interesting bugs were all in its parser. Chrome and Node disagree about how to read a malformed hostname, and no test could catch it, because the tests run on Node.

seeAlso.text: How that was found is in Writing

features.imageAlt: The SERP Reader card: a Google results page with the extension's Collect button over it.

roles.title: Founding Engineer
points: Founding engineer and sole developer of Dekho (dekho.shop), a live-shopping app on Android: sellers show the real thing live, and buyers ask anything and put in their own price.

roles.title: Software Developer
points: Designed and built KeySignals (keysignals.tech), the company's AI platform for SEO and Generative Engine Optimization, end to end as the only engineer, owning frontend, backend and integrations. Now live.

Architected a pipeline of 23 AI agents, coordinated by a queue-backed orchestrator on BullMQ and Redis, covering crawling, competitor and keyword research, clustering, content planning, writing, SEO and GEO optimization, and publishing.
Routed Claude, OpenAI and Gemini per task on quality, latency and cost, grounding every page in a business profile drawn from the site's own pages rather than the model's memory.

Built the GEO engine that tracks whether a brand is mentioned or cited in ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and AI Mode, plus a weekly Search Console and GA4 loop that drafts fixes for slipping pages and holds them for approval.

Added off-site GEO tooling that finds Reddit threads and GitHub discussions in a brand's category through Google's index rather than scraping, and exposed a public API and an MCP server for external tools and AI agents.
Built the control plane in Next.js 14: 67 dashboard screens on PostgreSQL, Redis and BullMQ, multi-tenant with NextAuth, JWT and role-based access control.

Before KeySignals, built the backend for the official MasterChef platform (masterchefworld.app) from scratch as the sole backend developer, on Node.js, Express and MongoDB across 6 REST domains, 30 route modules and 68 data models.

Engineered real-time event flow over WebSockets that keeps contestants in sync with a Twitch livestream despite per-viewer delay, and migrated 350,000+ existing users onto the new system with zero downtime and no data loss.
Built a 41-screen React and TypeScript admin console, integrated AWS S3, SES, Mux and Firebase, and maintained the app alongside KeySignals.

roles.title: Freelance Full-Stack Developer
points: Independently delivered a full-stack product for a 30,000+ member esports community, from architecture to deployment in two months.
Discord and Google OAuth with JWT sessions, plus three core modules — teams, tournaments, scrims — with approval workflows, RBAC, audit logging and a ban system.

writing.title: Narrowing stops at a function declaration
writing.description: TypeScript keeps a narrowed type inside an arrow function and loses it inside a hoisted function declaration. Measured across eight compiler versions.
writing.standfirst: Seven errors appeared in one component the day type checking was switched on, under a guard that was correct. The difference between the lines that failed and the lines that passed was one keyword.

writing.title: Chrome and Node disagree about this URL
writing.description: The same malformed hostname parses to a clean domain in Node and a punycoded mess in Chrome. A bug no test could catch, because the suite runs on Node.
writing.standfirst: It cost me the number one result twice, and no test could have caught it — because the test suite runs on Node, where the bug does not exist.
